To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the content of nucleic acid and proteins in the brain of rats reared in an information-enough medium is significantly higher than in the rats of the control and impoverished groups, while the RNA/DNA and Protein/DNA ratios in different brain structures are significantly higher in the rats of information-enriched group than in the control and deprived groups.
the RNA/DNA and RNA/Protein ratios in the brain of rats raised in an information enriched environment is higher than in rats raised in an impoverished environment.

the RNA/DNA and the protein/DNA ratio, as well as the RNA and protein content in the brain structures are more stable in ontogenetic development, while the RNA/DNA, protein/DNA and protein content are more sensitive to the afferentation level.
In summary, our research is concerned with

changes in nucleic acid content, RNA/DNA ratio and protein content in the rat brain at different stages of ontogenesis in the norm and in conditions of ecological deprivation and in information-enriched conditions.
the study of the influence of the ecological environment on the nucleic acid and proteins metabolism of different brain structures and the liver at different stages of ontogenesis.
the fact that the RNA/DNA and Protein/DNA ratio are the most sensitive indicators of the state of the central nervous system in conditions of different levels of afferentation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the changes observed in nucleic acid content are the most sensitive indicator of the brain activity level in the environment.

in conditions of information-enriched afferentation, which is accompanied with intensive brain activity, the RNA/DNA and RNA/protein ratios in all the studied structures of the rat brain increase in the early stages of postnatal development, which is indicative of the intensification of the synthesis of the protein component of the brain tissue.

the RNA/DNA and Protein/DNA ratio in the brain structures of rats reared in the information-enriched environment are substantially greater, while in those reared in the impoverished environment they are significantly smaller, than in the norm, i.e. in the rats reared in standard conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain cells in conditions of information enrichment are more active in their functional state, while in the conditions of ecological deprivation they are less active.

the changes in RNA/DNA and RNA/Protein ratios are more indicative of the brain activity level in the norm and in pathological conditions than the changes of the absolute content of nucleic acid and proteins in the nerve tissue.

the changes in RNA/DNA and RNA/protein ratio in the brain cells in conditions of ecological deprivation and in the information enriched environment, as well as in ontogenesis, are a reflection of the intensity of the cells physiological function.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the content of RNA and protein in the brain tissue of rats reared in an information-en-riched medium is higher than in the animals reared in an impoverished environment, which may indicate the importance of information for the normal development of brain cells.

in conditions of ecological deprivation the RNA/DNA and RNA/protein ratios in the brain cells diminish, and in conditions of an information-enrichment medium they grow, indicating a more intense synthesis of RNA and protein.
the changes in the nucleic acid and proteins content in the brain structures of rats reared in information-enriched environment is due to the stimulation of the transcribing activity of their genome.
